prompt: Why does mcp_host.py name each tool server__tool?

choices.text: To keep same-named tools apart
choices.why: Right. Two servers' tools with one name cannot collide: lesson 12's two get_order tools would get two names here.

choices.text: Because the Messages API requires a double underscore in every tool name
choices.why: Lesson 4's tools had none.

choices.text: Because the servers send their tools named that way
choices.why: The servers send get_order and refund; the host renames them.

choices.text: To hide the server from the model
choices.why: It does the opposite: the model sees which server.

prompt: When does mcp_host.py skip asking a person before a call?

choices.text: When the model says the call is safe
choices.why: The model's opinion is not consulted.

choices.text: When the tool is read-only and its server's hints are trusted
choices.why: Right. Only shop's tools qualify.

choices.text: Always, for the first call of a run, and then for every call that follows the same tool
choices.why: No such rule exists in the host.

choices.text: When the server declares elicitation
choices.why: Servers do not declare elicitation; clients do.

prompt: What did the model's tool list say about where each tool came from?

choices.text: Nothing; MCP tools look like any other
choices.why: The names and descriptions said so.

choices.text: Only the read-only hint
choices.why: Hints were not sent to the model.

choices.text: The server's address and process id, for each of the three server tools
choices.why: Neither was sent.

choices.text: The server's name
choices.why: Right. In the tool name and in the description; read_help, the host's own, has no server label.

prompt: How many tools did the host offer the model?
Why did search_help fail with the first, minimal ENV?

choices.text: Because labllm was down
choices.why: No model call was involved in the failure.

choices.text: Because PATH was missing
choices.why: PATH was in the list.

choices.text: MINILM_DIR was missing
choices.why: Right. It finds the embedding model; without it, the module looked in a directory that does not exist here.

choices.text: Because the help centre's forty articles were deleted when the lab was reset
choices.why: help://h14 was read in the same run.

prompt: Where was the reason for the search_help failure?

choices.text: In the tool result the model read
choices.why: That said only 'Error executing tool search_help'.

choices.text: In host.err, where the servers' standard error went
choices.why: Right. A host that discards it discards the reason.

choices.text: In host-audit.jsonl, which records the traceback of every failed call
choices.why: The audit has is_error, not tracebacks.

choices.text: In labllm's log
choices.why: labllm saw only the model's requests.

prompt: What stopped the model's request to read file:///home/ana/agents/data/shop.db?

choices.text: The shop server, which refused the URI
choices.why: The request never reached a server.

choices.text: The operating system's file permissions
choices.why: ana can read that file.

choices.text: The model, which changed its mind
choices.why: The refusal came back as an error result.

choices.text: The host's check that only help:// URIs are read
choices.why: Right. Before any server was asked.

prompt: Why does the scheme check belong in the host, although the shop server serves only help:// anyway?

choices.text: Because servers cannot refuse URIs
choices.why: They can; this one would have.

choices.text: Relying on the server means trusting every server with the same care
choices.why: Right. The host is where the request becomes an action.

choices.text: Because the check is faster in the host
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: Because MCP forbids servers from reading files, so only hosts may touch the file system
choices.why: MCP forbids nothing of the kind.

prompt: Why was the person asked twice about the approved refund?

choices.text: Because the first answer was lost
choices.why: Both answers were read.

choices.text: Because the model asked again
choices.why: The model called refund once.

choices.text: The host asked, then the server
choices.why: Right. The host's policy first, then the server's own code: two rules with two owners.

choices.text: Because MCP requires two confirmations for any tool whose annotations do not say read-only
choices.why: No such requirement exists.

prompt: When the person answered n to the host, what did the refunds server see?

choices.text: Nothing; the call never reached it
choices.why: Right. The model read the host's refusal.

choices.text: A tools/call with approval set to false
choices.why: approval is filled by the server's own question.

choices.text: An input_required result
choices.why: That is something a server sends, not receives.

choices.text: A cancellation notice
choices.why: Nothing was sent.

prompt: How many lines did host-audit.jsonl hold at the end of the lesson's runs?
Which of these does the host's audit record that a server's own log could not? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: The declined refund
choices.why: Right. It never reached the server.

choices.text: The refused file:// URI
choices.why: Right. No server was asked.

choices.text: Calls to both servers, in one place
choices.why: Right. Only the host sees every server.

choices.text: The server's traceback
choices.why: Tracebacks go to the server's standard error.

prompt: Why can a server connected to mcp_host.py not ask the host's model to write text?

choices.text: Because labllm refuses requests from servers
choices.why: Servers never reach labllm.

choices.text: Because the server has no API key
choices.why: Sampling does not use the server's key.

choices.text: Because stdio cannot carry such requests
choices.why: It is a matter of capabilities, not of transport.

choices.text: The host gave its Client no sampling callback
choices.why: Right. So the client does not declare sampling.

prompt: What does input_required_max_rounds protect the host against?

choices.text: A server that keeps answering input_required, holding the call forever
choices.why: Right. The loop stops after a fixed number of rounds.

choices.text: A model that calls too many tools
choices.why: That is MAX_STEPS, the host's own limit.

choices.text: A person who answers too slowly
choices.why: There is no timeout on the person in this host.

choices.text: A tampered requestState
choices.why: The server's seal handles that.
